thread.title: Apple's stock goes ex-dividend, slips toward 1st loss in 10 days - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Apple's stock goes ex-dividend, slips toward 1st loss in 10 days - MarketWatch
text: Apple Inc.'s stock AAPL, -0.43% slipped 0.4% in morning trade Friday, putting it in danger of suffering its first loss in 10 sessions. The nine-session win streak through Thursday, which was the longest such streak since the nine-day stretch ending July 19, 2017 , and Thursday's fifth-straight record close, were fueled by better-than-expected earnings and an endorsement from famed billionaire value investor Warren Buffett . The stock closed at a record $190.04 on Thursday. For those wondering why, with the stock trading at $188.74, some quoting services say its trading down just 57 cents from $189.31, it's because the stock went ex-dividend. That means the quoting services adjusted the close to reflect the payout of a 73-cent quarterly dividend. The stock has rallied 11.6% year to date, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.11% has gained 0.4%.
